title: Issues, Projects and Team Habits —

header.html: Use issues, labels, assignees, milestones and templates; use project boards and Discussions; write good commit messages; install a commit-msg hook; keep PRs small and review well; write a CONTRIBUTING file; handle large files; find changes with blame, log -S and bisect
Git 2.50.1 for the local parts; the GitHub documentation (read 2026-11-16) for the GitHub parts

toc.title: Good commit messages and a commit-msg hook
Small pull requests and review etiquette

html:
1Issues, projects and Discussions

Teams stay in step when work is visible. An issue tracks one bug, task or question. A good issue has a title that names the problem, the steps to reproduce it, and what you expected instead.

Feature What it gives you
Labels Categories such as bug, docs or an area of the code; you filter by them
Assignees The person who owns the work
Milestones A group of issues for one release or date
Templates A form of questions that every new issue starts from

A PR that says Closes #42 closes the issue when it merges into the default branch (module 9). A project board lays out issues and PRs by status, so everyone sees what is waiting, in progress or done. Discussions hold open questions and ideas that are not tasks yet. When a discussion turns into work, open an issue.

Tip

. One issue, one outcome. If an issue needs "and also" in its title, split it, so each PR can close exactly one issue.

2Good commit messages and a commit-msg hook

History is read far more often than it is written, so write for the reader six months from now.

Part Habit
Subject About 50 characters, imperative ("Add", "Fix"), no final period
Blank line Always separates the subject from the body
Body Wrapped at about 72 characters; explain why, because the diff shows what
Footer References such as Closes #42

Conventional Commits add a type to the subject: feat, fix, docs, refactor, test or chore, optionally with a scope, as in fix(cart): round the total.

Try it. Write a commit with a subject, a body and a footer, then read it back.

git commit -m "fix: round the cart total half up" -m "Totals were rounded down, so some carts showed a cent too little.
Round half up to match the payment provider." -m "Closes #42"
git log -1 --format=%B

fix: round the cart total half up

Totals were rounded down, so some carts showed a cent too little.
Round half up to match the payment provider.

Closes #42

A commit-msg hook is a script that Git runs after you write the message. It receives the path of the message file, and a non-zero exit cancels the commit.

Git hooks live in .git/hooks, which is not cloned. Keep the script in a tracked folder such as .githooks, mark it executable in the index with git update-index --chmod=+x, and let each clone run git config core.hooksPath .githooks once.

Try it. This hook allows only the six types and at most 72 characters, and lets merge and revert messages through.

#!/bin/sh
# .githooks/commit-msg: allow "type: summary", 72 characters at most
subject=$(head -n 1 "$1")
case "$subject" in Merge\ *|Revert\ *) exit 0 ;; esac
pattern='^(feat|fix|docs|refactor|test|chore)(\([a-z0-9-]+\))?: .+'
if [ ${#subject} -le 72 ] && echo "$subject" | grep -Eq "$pattern"; then exit 0; fi
echo "Rejected: use 'type: summary' (feat, fix, docs, refactor, test or chore)." >&2
exit 1

Try it. Switch the hook on, then commit with a bad subject.

git config core.hooksPath .githooks
git commit -m "fixed stuff"

Rejected: use 'type: summary' (feat, fix, docs, refactor, test or chore).

No commit is made. Tested here: a good subject is accepted, a subject over 72 characters is rejected, and a fresh clone has no hook until core.hooksPath is set. git commit --no-verify skips the hook, so a hook helps but does not enforce: the real gate is a server-side check.

Tip

. Explain why in the body, not what. Anyone can read the diff, but only you know the reason for the change.

3Small pull requests and review etiquette

A small PR has one purpose and can be read in minutes. It gets faster and better reviews, is easier to test, and is easier to undo. If the description needs "and also", split it.

A reviewer checks, in this order:

  1. Does the change do what the description and the issue say?
  2. Is it correct, tested and readable, and do the checks succeed?
  3. Does it touch anything it should not, such as unrelated files, secrets or large files?

Write comments about the code, not the person. Ask a question rather than give an order. Say why, and suggest an alternative. Mark a minor taste as optional, for instance with "nit:". Say what is good too. Use Request changes only for real blockers, and Approve when the rest is minor. Authors answer every comment and push fixes as new commits.

A CONTRIBUTING.md file in the repository tells newcomers how to propose changes: branch names, commit style, how to run the tests and what review to expect.

Large files make every clone slower, because Git keeps every version of every file. Git LFS (Large File Storage) stores small pointer files in the repository and the real content on a separate server. You pick files with git lfs track and commit the .gitattributes file it writes. The course does not run it.

Tip

. Split a PR that cannot be reviewed in one sitting. Smaller changes get faster and better reviews.

4Debugging history as a team

Three commands answer "who, when and which commit". git blame -L 3,4 file shows who last changed lines 3 to 4. git log -S"text" lists commits that added or removed that text. git bisect run finds the first bad commit by binary search with a test script.

Try it. Blame two lines, then search for the text that was removed. Your hashes and dates will differ.

git blame -L 3,4 --date=relative total.sh
git log -S"rate=20" --oneline

cf3813f7 (bob 2 minutes ago 3) rate=2
057062cf (ada 3 minutes ago 4) echo $(( $1 * $2 * (100 + rate) / 100 ))
cf3813f Tidy the tax rate setting
057062c Add the total script

Blame shows who last touched a line, not who caused the bug, so read the commit. The -S search found both the commit that added rate=20 and the one that removed it.

Try it. test.sh fails on the newest commit. Mark the bad and the good commit, and let Git search.

git bisect start HEAD HEAD~5
git bisect run sh test.sh

running 'sh' 'test.sh'
Bisecting: 0 revisions left to test after this (roughly 0 steps)
[bb21fdf61262fd29b0c0135d28ccd21e6db24d46] Add usage notes
running 'sh' 'test.sh'
cf3813f73e23a238c563b89a28119cd7794baa55 is the first bad commit
Author: bob <bob@example.com>

    Tidy the tax rate setting

The test script must exist at every commit that bisect checks out, or live outside the repository. It exits 0 for good and non-zero, such as 1, for bad. Exit code 125 means "skip this commit": if the neighbor of the bad commit is skipped, bisect lists both commits as suspects. Finish with git bisect reset.

Tip

. Write the failing test first, then run git bisect run. A script that exits 0 or 1 turns hours of guessing into a few automatic steps.

5Practice Q&A

5.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1A teammate asks which subject line follows the team habits. Which one is best?

  • AFixed rounding bugs in the cart total.
  • Bfix: round the cart total half up
  • Cupdated some files for the cart total
  • DWIP cart total rounding changes today
Show the answer

Answer: B. It has a known type, an imperative summary, a short length and no final period.

S2Ada's commit-msg hook rejects bad subjects, but Bob's fresh clone accepts them. What is the cause and the fix?

  • A.git/hooks is not cloned; commit a hooks folder and set core.hooksPath
  • BHooks run only for the person who first created the repository on GitHub
  • CThe hook is cloned but runs only for commits made on the main branch
  • DHooks start working after one git commit --no-verify run is made
Show the answer

Answer: A. The hooks folder is local to each clone, so the team shares a tracked folder and points Git at it.

S3git blame -L 3,4 total.sh shows line 3 as cf3813f7 (bob 3) rate=2. What does that tell you?

  • ABob wrote the whole file, so every line has the same author
  • BBob's commit is proven to be the cause of the failing test
  • CBob must fix the line because he is now the owner of that line
  • DBob's commit last changed line 3, so read that commit next
Show the answer

Answer: D. Blame names the last commit to touch a line, which is a lead, not a verdict.

S4You need every commit that added or removed the text rate=20. Which command does that?

  • Agit blame rate=20, which lists all of the commits that mention the text
  • Bgit bisect rate=20, which searches all of the history for the text
  • Cgit log -S"rate=20", which finds commits that change the text
  • Dgit log --grep="rate=20", which searches the contents of the files
Show the answer

Answer: C. The -S search finds commits where the number of occurrences of the text changes.

S5A PR changes 1,800 lines across three unrelated features, and the checks are green. What is the best review response?

  • AAsk the author to split it into small single-purpose PRs
  • BApprove it quickly, because green checks prove it is correct
  • CRequest changes on every file, to be on the safe side
  • DMerge it now and review the details after the release
Show the answer

Answer: A. Small, single-purpose PRs get better reviews and are easy to revert.

S6Designers commit large source files, and every clone slows down. What helps most?

  • ARebase the repository so that the files vanish from its history
  • BRun git gc once a day in each teammate's clone of the repository
  • CTrack the files with Git LFS so the repo holds small pointers
  • DSquash every PR so that the files are stored only once
Show the answer

Answer: C. LFS keeps pointer files in the repository and the large content on a separate server.

5.2 Recall questions

R1What are the usual limits for the subject and the body of a commit message?

Show the answer

About 50 characters for the subject and about 72 characters per body line.

R2Which six Conventional Commits types does this course use?

Show the answer

feat, fix, docs, refactor, test and chore.

R3How does a team share a commit-msg hook?

Show the answer

Commit it in a folder such as .githooks, and run git config core.hooksPath .githooks in each clone.

R4Which command shows who last changed lines 3 and 4 of a file?

Show the answer

git blame -L 3,4 file.

R5What do the exit codes of a git bisect run script mean?

Show the answer

0 is good, a non-zero code such as 1 is bad, and 125 skips the commit.

R6Which option skips a commit-msg hook?

Show the answer

git commit --no-verify.

6Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Issues labels, assignees, milestones, templates; one issue, one outcome
Boards and Discussions boards show status; Discussions hold open questions and ideas
Commit message subject about 50 characters, imperative; blank line; body about 72, explains why
Conventional Commits feat, fix, docs, refactor, test, chore
commit-msg hook non-zero exit cancels the commit; not cloned; use core.hooksPath; --no-verify skips
Small PRs one purpose; reviewer checks intent, correctness and side effects
Review comments about the code; question, reason, alternative; optional for taste
Large files Git LFS keeps pointers in the repository, content elsewhere
Debugging history git blame -L, git log -S, git bisect run with exit 0, 1 or 125
